briefs.source_chain: Buffers that used to absorb oil shocks (strong US exports, weak Chinese demand, ample inventories) are fading while supply disruptions converge, therefore WTI/Brent spike and SPR hits a 1984 low, therefore MS abandons its benign de-escalation baseline for an oil risk-premium baseline (45% probability), therefore core PCE/GDP/consumption forecasts are revised and MS now expects two more 25bp hikes to a 4.25-4.50% terminal, driven partly by Warsh's hawkish framing and the neutral-rate revision.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain: fading buffers + converging supply disruptions -> oil price spike + SPR at 1984 low -> shift to oil risk-premium baseline (45%) -> revised core PCE/GDP/consumption/investment/labor forecasts -> two more 25bp hikes to 4.25-4.50% terminal, citing Warsh and the neutral-rate revision.

briefs.source_chain: The FOMC hiked 25bp unanimously and swapped its supply-shock inflation language for a 'timelier return to 2%' pledge, therefore the SEP (unemployment down to 4.1%, core PCE up to 3.4%, upside-only inflation risk, no downside employment risk) confirms the Committee sees low stagflation risk and is focused on inflation, therefore the 2026 dot implies 50bp more this year and the long-run dot rose to 3.2%, and Warsh's 'not restrictive/removing accommodation' framing plus the SEP support SG's existing call for two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March) to unwind the 2025 insurance cuts, conditional on inflation data.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures and same conditional framing.

briefs.source_chain: The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.0%; Warsh's 'removing accommodation' framing, his geopolitics/oil emphasis, and the neutral-rate revision to 3.25% from 3.06% together tilt MS toward two more 25bp hikes (Dec, March) to a 4.25-4.50% terminal in 1Q27, with an October hike not ruled out and de-escalation/faster disinflation as the downside risk to just one more hike; rates/FX/MBS/munis desks each attach a specific trade idea to this read.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain, same figures (8 of 18 seeing a third 2027 hike, neutral rate 3.25% from 3.06%), same October-hike and de-escalation hedges, same four-desk trade-idea attribution.

briefs.source_chain: DM equity buying (led by US Tech and a fast European short-cover rally) was funded by Asia selling while Mag-7/Software flows recovered; GS (via Oppenheimer) stays constructive medium-term since compute demand outstripping supply lowers earnings-bubble risk, keeping SPX EPS growth at 11% for 2027/2028; separately, China's Go Global (30% entry discount, price recovery in 7/11 sectors, ex-China share rising 18%->31% by 2035, upside unpriced) and India's 42 AI-infrastructure names (+60% YTD vs NIFTY -11%, ~40% of NIFTY 500 capex growth) are flagged as under-appreciated theses.
briefs.brief_chain: Same chain and same figures throughout; brief omits the secondary MTD Asia HF rotation detail (Korea/Taiwan/Japan to HK/China) and the 2Q EPS growth/'over-earning' aside, neither of which changes any stance or figure.

distortions.what: Brief drops the secondary MTD Asia HF flow detail (rotation from Korea/Taiwan/Japan into HK/China) and the 2Q SPX EPS growth ('50% YoY, 26% 4Q trailing, some over-earning signs but not a bubble') aside
distortions.would_the_trade_change: No — these are supporting color for the same constructive stance already carried by the 11% EPS growth figure and the China/India theses; nothing about direction, conviction, or targets changes.
